intro: Professionals and everyday users convert atmospheres (atm) to bars (bar) when working across other and metric standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One standard atmosphere equals 1.01325 bars, while 1 bar equals 0.986923 atmospheres. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between atm and bar. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many bars (bar) are in 1 standard atmosphere (atm)?
faqs.answer: There are 1.01325 bars (bar) in 1 standard atmosphere (atm), which rounds to 1.0133 bar for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 bar equals 0.986923 atmospheres.

faqs.question: How do I convert atmospheres to bars (atm to bar)?
faqs.answer: To convert atmospheres to bars, use the formula: bar = atm × 1.01325. For example, converting 2.2 atm gives 2.2292 bar.

faqs.question: What is 2.2 atmospheres in bars?
faqs.answer: 2.2 atmospheres (atm) equals exactly 2.2292 bars (bar) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
